meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee reviewed issues submitted by private individuals. Information regarding the loan agreement signed between the Government of the Maldives and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to borrow USD 50,000,000 (Fifty Million) required for the "Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project" to be implemented in the Maldives with assistance from the bank. Information regarding the sovereign guarantee issued by the Government for Maldives Industrial Fisheries Company Limited (MIFCO) to secure a demand loan facility of USD 44,000,000 (Forty-Four million) and an overdraft facility of MVR 200,000,000 (Two Hundred Million) through the Bank of Maldives, to manage the company's cash flow requirements and repay loans obtained through SME Digital. Information regarding the guarantee issued by the Government of Maldives for the facility signed by Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL) with Vitol APAC Capital Private Limited (Vitol) to secure a facility of USD 28,000,000 (Twenty-Eight million). Lastly in the meeting, the following letters received by the Committee were shared with the members: Letter sent by the Auditor General's Office stating that it has obtained membership on the Board of the INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI)—the capacity-building arm of the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI)—for the first time. Atoll Hospital. Letter sent by an individual citizen to the Prosecutor General's Office and copied to the People's Majlis Secretariat, regarding the issue of the HA. meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee addressed a public grievance concerning a Ministry of Finance and Planning directive. The directive seeks to cease living allowances for employees of the Information Commissioner’s Office and recover payments made over the past 1 year and 10 months. It was decided to agenda this matter for a future meeting once members have had sufficient time to review the details. Subsequently, the Committee deliberated on two issues submitted by private individuals. The first issue concerns the discontinuation of the 20-year service pension for individuals upon reaching the age of 65, including a request to meet with the Speaker of the Parliament, the Deputy Speaker, and the relevant committee. The second issue involves a proposal to establish a retirement scheme that would allow members of the National Integrity Commission to retire before the end of their official terms. Following the discussion, it was decided that the secretariat would gather further information regarding these matters, after which they will be formally scheduled for a committee meeting. The Auditor General’s Office 2025 financial statements were shared with the committee. Additionally, the committee reviewed the 2025 Annual Reports of the National Pay Commission and the Ministry of Finance and Planning. It was decided that identified areas for improvement would be communicated to these institutions in writing. The committee deliberated public concerns regarding delayed audit reports for government institutions and the long-standing failure to resolve issues highlighted in these reports. During the discussion South Hulhumale' Constituency member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed proposed to send a formal inquiry to the Ministry of Finance and Public Enterprises to clarify the following matters. 1. The underlying rationale behind the government’ s decision to terminate 33% of State-Owned Enterprises employees. 2. To request that a comprehensive document detailing the current financial status of State-Owned Enterprises be shared with the Committee. Although the motion was seconded by Hanimaadhoo Constituency member Abdul Gafoor Moosa, the proposal was not passed. Additionally, the process of appointing a member to the sub-committee established to review the audit reports of Fenaka Corporation Limited was carried out. In this regard, the proposal made by Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh and seconded by South Hulhumale' Constituency member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed to appoint Eydhafushi Constituency member Ahmed Saleem to the committee was passed unanimously by the committee. meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee had discussions with officials from the Maldives Pension Administration Office and the Civil Service Commission regarding other retirement benefits provided outside of the pension benefits granted under the Retirement Pension Scheme as stipulated in Law No. 8/2009 (Maldives Pension Act). The officials from Maldives Pension Administration Office raised their concern that there are people who does not want to participate in the retirement pension scheme because of the other retirement benefits provided outside of the pension benefits granted under the Retirement Pension Scheme. Moreover, the official suggested that while abolishing the benefits provided by schemes operated by individual institutions outside of that Retirement Pension Scheme, instead of sudden abolition, moderate solutions need to be found. Furthermore, the official from the Civil Service Commission noted that some people continue to work in other institutions outside the civil service after retiring from the civil service. The official stated that this is not an acceptable practice under any circumstances, and they believe that a solution to this issue should be found through legislation. Based on the information shared by the Civil Service Commission and Maldives Pension Administration Office, committee requested to provide a timeline on the work to bring the necessary amendments to the law.

meetings.title: 6th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The committee sat with the below mentioned from Ministry of Finance to discuss regarding the Financial and Economic state of the country. Dr. Mohamed Shafeeq, Minister Ahmed Saeed Musthafa, Deputy Minister Mohamed Azad, Accountant General Fathimath Mohamed Didi, Debt Management Executive Ahmed Zayan Mohamed, Economist During the meeting, the committee discussed regarding government's debt and public expenditure along with the ministry's efforts to reduce these expenditures. The minister informed that in order to reduce the expenditures, the ministry would undertake reforms of state-owned companies, a plan on the order for PSIP projects to be commenced based on the availability and importance would be implemented and the government plans on the changes to be brought in the subsidies. The ministry also informed that the implementation of the recommendations made by the ministry with the committee regarding increasing revenue will begin after the ministry's plans for reforms to reduce public expenditure are completed.
